text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Minister of communications says parliamentarians should support the state in reductions in its expatriate workforce.
- National Real Estate Company says third-quarter net profit rose 64.06 percent to 2.5 million dinars ($8.3 million) compared to the same period in 1995.
- Minister of Finance Nasser al-Rodhan says state of economy satisfying.
- Customs authorities to keep close watch on goods imported form south-east Asian countries in a crack down on counterfeits.
- Kuwait Finance House official wants more economic openess.
- Kuwait to build comprehensive general service centres in its five governorates in 1997.
- Kuwait's food industry products suffer competition from Gulf made products, industrialists say.
- Kuwait National Petroleum Company says refineries total output capacity to rise to 890,000 barrels per day from 852.000 in January of 1997.

- Parliamentarians propose a bill to subsidise private sector wages for Kuwaitis. Most of the national workforce is hired by the state. The private sector depends largely on expatriates who make up more than half of the 2.0 million population.
- Interior ministry mulls increasing visitor permits duration to three months from one month.
